claims.text: The starting material is a powder blend of Group IV elements Hf, Zr, and Ti and Group V elements V, Nb, and Ta with trace C, N, and O impurities.
Group IV-V RHEA feedstocks tend to develop compositional striations.
Slow cooling of Group IV-V RHEAs promotes brittle intermetallic formation.
High-volumetric-energy-density SLM can produce a single-phase solid solution.
Immediate water quenching or cryogenic cooling after SLM bypasses equilibrium phase separation.
Processing under argon with oxygen below 10 ppm is required for the proposed route.
Post-processing cooling rates above 1000 K/s suppress diffusion-controlled precipitation.
The targeted microstructural state is a metastable single-phase BCC solid solution.
Configurational entropy of mixing stabilizes the BCC solid solution against phase separation.
Rapid cooling prevents formation of brittle sigma or Laves phases.
Rapid cooling retains interstitial impurities in a supersaturated solid solution.
A VEC below 4.4 improves the stability or mechanical performance of W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf RHEAs.
The combined rapid thermal histories of SLM and quenching kinetically trap the alloy in a single-phase BCC state.
Rapid processing prevents interstitial impurities from diffusing to grain boundaries.
Interstitial segregation at grain boundaries would cause embrittlement in the proposed alloy.
SLM followed by rapid quenching will produce a homogeneous single-phase BCC microstructure in the proposed RHEA.
The processed alloy will retain high yield strength at temperatures up to 1000°C.
The processed alloy will be significantly less brittle than conventionally cast counterparts.
Suppressing phase separation and brittle-phase formation will improve high-temperature structural integrity.
Conventionally cast or slowly cooled Group IV-V RHEAs typically have BCC plus sigma or Laves microstructures, substantial segregation, and brittle failure caused by interstitial clustering.

contradictions.description: The initial alloy family is defined using only Group IV elements Hf/Zr/Ti and Group V elements V/Nb/Ta, whereas the mechanistic analogy and proposed experiment use W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf. W and Cr are Group VI elements, so the experimental system does not match the stated Group IV-V-only family.
